source.title: Decisions in Changing Conditions: The Urgency-Gating Model

confidence_rationale: The cleanest computational grounding that WHEN to commit is a governed, time-varying control parameter rather than a fixed threshold: evidence is multiplied by a growing urgency signal, so the effective decision criterion drops over time and commitment timing is tunable. This is the mechanistic backbone of MECH-434 (commitment timing as the axis whose two poles are freezing and panic). Held at 0.74 because it is a model of perceptual two-choice decisions, not of REE's belief-state-over-trajectories commitment, and urgency here is motor-related rather than threat-driven.
failure_signatures: A fixed (non-urgency) bound cannot adapt commitment timing to changing conditions -- it either over-deliberates (freezing) or commits prematurely; urgency-gating shows timing is an adjustable gain, which is exactly what the two MECH-434 poles dysregulate in opposite directions.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In changing environments the brain does not integrate evidence to a fixed bound; it multiplies a (low-pass-filtered) estimate of momentary sensory evidence by a growing urgency signal, so the effective decision criterion decreases with time -- a built-in, adjustable trade-off between decision speed and accuracy.
mapping.ree_translation: Grounds MECH-434's core assertion that commitment timing is a GOVERNED control parameter, not an emergent side-effect: the urgency signal is the biological analogue of the knob REE would tune at the seam between the belief-state set (MECH-385) / epistemic action pressure (MECH-388) and the commitment gate (MECH-061/MECH-090). Epistemic-freezing = urgency held too low / threshold too high; anti-epistemic-panic = urgency forced too high / threshold collapsed.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Urgency-gating is modelled for rapid perceptual two-alternative choices with motor-related urgency; REE's commitment is over inferred trajectories under partial observability with threat-/goal-driven (not motor) urgency. The transferable claim is the EXISTENCE of an adjustable timing parameter, not the specific multiplicative urgency mechanism.
mapping.source_context: Computational model + monkey/human reaching decisions under changing sensory evidence.

confidence_components.notes: Strong J Neurosci source. Mapping fidelity good for 'timing is a tunable parameter'; transfer risk moderate (perceptual-motor -> trajectory-commitment).
